This procedure details the items, which are checked every two years. They
 include testing and major maintenance. In addition to the procedures listed,
 it is expected the checks, which are done more frequently, would also be
 completed at this time.
Work permit must be issued, the qualified maintenance staff must carry the suitable ID safety category,
Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the work area is required,

 air.

sections.text: Tension Adjusting Roller (No. 59) of the Belt (Fig 2)

items: Release the grease cup (65).
Release the tension adjusting roller screw and remove the two belts.
Remove the axial shaft of the tension-adjusting roller.
Remove the two ball bearings from the shaft.
Clean and check them and change if needed.
Collect the tension-adjusting roller and grease the ball bearings.

items:
Unscrew the six nuts of the cylinder cover studs and raise the
 cover (4 fig 1) up and the central nut of the cover (socket wrench 17),
 which connecting between cylinder head and valve.
Remove the valve boards (3 fig1) and remove the two gaskets (No 8 fig 1).

Unscrew the two fitted bolts (No3 fig 3) and raise the upper valve board
 (2 fig 3) up.

Remove the suction plates (No. 6 fig 3) then remove the delivery plates (
 No.8 fig 3).
Clean all valve parts with benzene.

Make smoothing to the upper and lower board surfaces of the valve using
 very fine grinding past.
Clean the upper and lower boards surfaces of the valve.

Put the suction and delivery plates in their places and check its
 clearances (must be not more than 0.2 mm) OR replace if needed.

Remove the cotter pin that fix the two nuts of the end of the
 connecting rod to the crankshaft (50 fig 2) and unscrew the two nuts.

Remove the half bearing of the connecting rod, pull out the first stage
 piston, and the connecting rod.

Unscrew the four nuts of the studs that fixed the first stage cylinder (1)
 to the crank case (N0. 32) if needed and clean the inner surface with
 benzene and dry it

Pull out the piston pen to separate the piston (No 2) from its connecting
 rod.

Change the two copper bearings of the piston, the copper bearings of small
 end of the connecting rod, and check the connecting rod alloy.

Remove the four rings (No 9) of the piston: (3) compression and (1) oil
 wiper.
Clean the piston with benzene and change the four rings.
Remove the two crank case hatch covers (no.35).

items:

 the third stage cylinder cover 10 fig 3

Unscrew the nut (8fig7) and remove the body, upper portion (1fig 7)

Remove the circular suction plate (3fig 7) and delivery circular plate
 (5fig7).

Remove the suction valve spring (2fig 7) and delivery valve spring (6fig
 7)

Clean all parts of the valve and clean all suction and delivery plates
 holes.

Make smoothing to the suction and delivery circular plates with grinding
 paste.
Clean all parts with benzene and collect the valve.

Unscrew the four nuts of the studs that fixed the third stage
 cylinder (No 16) to the cross head cylinder (No 17) and raise the cylinder
 (No 16) up, and clean it with benzene.

Remove the cotter pin that fixed the two nuts of the end of the connecting
 rod to the crankshaft (No. 50 fig 4) and unscrew the two nuts.

Remove the half bearing of the connecting rod and pull out the third stage
 piston with its connecting rod.

Disconnect the two end plugs of the piston pin and pull out the piston pin
 to separate the cross head (No. 18) from its connecting rod.

Change the copper bearing of the cross head, the copper bearing of the
 small end of the connecting rod and check the connecting rod alloy.

Remove the 5 rings of the piston and clean it with benzene, and change the
 5 piston rings.

Unscrew the four screws that fixed the third stagpiston (No 15) to cross
 head (N0. 18), and pull it out.

Unscrew the four nuts of the studs that fixed the cross head cylinder (N0.
 17) to the crank case (No. 32) and clean the inner surface with benzene and
 dry it.

Unscrew the 4 screws that fix the flywheel cover to the
 compressor base and pullout the cover of the flywheel.

Unscrew the three screws (sp24) that fixing the flywheel to the crankshaft
 sleeve.
Pull out the flywheel (No 67) away from the crankshaft.
Pull out the sleeve with its key.

Disconnect the crankcase rear cover (79) and pull out the set of shims
 (80).
Disconnect the drive pulley (46) from the front end of the crankshaft.

Disconnect the crankcase front cover (44) by unscrewing 6 screws (sp17)
 and pull it out with its gasket (43).

Disconnect the rubber tube joint between the crankshaft and oil pump and
 disconnect the copper tube between the gauge filter (38) and the oil pump
 (40).

Disconnect the oil pump housing no. (No 41) with the oil pump and the
 vertical gear and the oil filter.
Disconnect the oil pump driving gear (No 54).
Pull out the oil distributing ring (49).
Pull out the set of shims (55).
Pull out the moving shell (57).

Pullout the crankshaft (50 fig 2, clean it, check any corrosions for its
 surface and its bearing alloys.
Disconnect the two counter weights (No 82) if needed and keep them away.
Change the two ball bearings from the crankshaft (50).

Disconnect the electrical connections of the motor and isolate
 it properly.

Disconnect the 10 coupling pins (No.69 ) with its rubber sleeves(No.68)
 using special tool to separate the engine half coupling (No.70) from the fly
 wheel (No 67)

Disconnect the four bolts of the motor (2 fig.7) to release the motor from
 the welded bed plate and keep it away.

Disconnect the back cover of the fan by unscrewing the 4 screws sp.17 and
 remove the fan key from the motor shaft then pull out the motor fan.

Unscrew the 8 screws that fix the cover of the back ball bearing and check
 the bearing then clean it with benzene and put new grease if it is in good
 condition.

Pull out the engine half coupling (No. 70) by pull out its feather key
 (No. 75) and disconnect the front cover of the front rolling bearing and
 check the bearings and change it if needed or clean it with benzene and put
 new grease if there are in good condition.
Reassemble the two bearings cover of the motor.
Reassemble the fan on the motor shaft and fix its cover.
Rotate the motor manually and check for any abnormal sounds.

Reassemble all parts of the compressor after changing all
 gaskets.

Crankshaft and its accessory oil pump, oil pump housing, crank case front
 cover, and drive pulley (46 fig.2).

Adjust the horizontal movement of the crank shaft by using the set of
 shims (80 fig.2)
Reassemble the flywheel to the crankshaft.
Reassemble the motor drive to the flywheel.
Check the rubber sleeves around the bolts of flywheel.
Check the 12 coupling pins and change any of them if needed.

Put the flywheel on the crank end and check the clearance between the
 flywheel and the engine half coupling (it must be 2 mm).

Reassemble the cylinders of the 3 stages to its places on the crankcase
 (32fig.1).

Reassemble completely the connecting rods to their pistons then reassemble
 them to the crank shaft starting with the third stage
Reassemble the valves and airheads of all stages.
Reassemble the fan and the cooler unit (radiator).

Disconnect the breather cover (31 fig.1) and refill the compressor with
 oil from the breather tube, refill the oil filter with oil and check
 manually the pump working.
Reassemble the air intake filter (fig.6) to the inlet of the 1st.stage.

Reassemble all air pipe connections (out let and inlet ) for all stages,
 Oil pump and radiators.
Connecting rods, pistons, cylinders, valves, air head of all stages.
All air pipe connection (out let and inlet) for all stages
Run the compressor manually and listen to any abnormal sound.
Run the compressor by the motor and listen to any abnormal sound.
Put the starting switch in ON position and operate the compressor.

Check every stage pressure on pressure gauges (fig. 5)
 First Stage 3 atm.
 Second Stage 12 atm.
 Third Stage 40 atm.
Check oil pressure (2:4 atm) on oil pressure gauge.
Check for any air or oil leakage.

Record the maintenance, which has-been done and all parts, which have been
 changed in maintenance card.
Record the number of operating hours
